correctness.rationale: For all m,n>=3 and strictly positive margins, a strict-support Hall argument gives all necessary and sufficient two-zero incidence inequalities. If strict support fails, a third forced coordinate zero has independent affine restriction because deleting at most three edges from K_{m,n} remains connected unless it isolates a positive-margin vertex. Frobenius projection P_m E_ij P_n yields the three exact normalized normal products. Central counts and arcsine asymptotics were reconstructed algebraically; 7,068 separate LP pair tests and exact rational Gram tests provide independent finite diagnostics but not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem computes every natural codimension-two metric angle and all incidence/multiplicity data of a broad classical convex body family, with a finite, exact margin-chamber decision procedure that needs no vertex enumeration; the central case has a sharp 3×3 obstruction and a nonuniform-integrability angle asymptotic.
